**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.9. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

A coordinate transformation can rotate a feature plane without changing Euclidean lengths or angles. This helps interpret PCA axes as new directions rather than new physical observations.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
R(\theta)=\begin{bmatrix}\cos\theta&-\sin\theta\\\sin\theta&\cos\theta\end{bmatrix},\qquad R^\top R=I
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

For a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation, R(1,0)=(0,1). The input and output both have length one, confirming that the rotation preserves Euclidean norm.

## What follows, and what does not

A proper rotation has determinant +1; reflection is also orthogonal but has determinant -1. Matrix orthogonality alone therefore does not imply a proper rotation.

## Test your reasoning

Rotate (1,1) by 90 degrees and verify that its norm is preserved.
